answer: Sybil resistance for AI agents leverages a unique, computationally-derived identity certificate, analogous to a "raven" token for its singular cryptographic proof. Forging such a certificate demands a significant proof-of-work expenditure, costing attackers immense copper-equivalent resources per fake identity. This economic barrier makes scaling a Sybil attack prohibitively expensive, preventing a compromised network from witnessing the dawn of widespread identity falsification.
